Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
#include<vector>
#include<algorithm>
#include<iostream>
using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    vector<int> sortedSquares(vector<int>& nums) {
        vector<int> squares;
        for (auto& num : nums) squares.push_back(num * num);
        if (nums.front() >= 0) return squares;
        if (nums.back() <= 0)
        {
            reverse(squares.begin(), squares.end());
            return squares;
        }
        sort(squares.begin(), squares.end());
        return squares;
    }
};
// Test
int main()
{
    Solution sol;
    vector<int> nums = {-4, -1, 0, 3, 10};
    auto res = sol.sortedSquares(nums);
    printf("%d ", res);
    return 0;
}
